To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lathyrogen treatment of rats with methylcholanthren induced fibrosarcomas reduced the total collagen content of the tumour by approximately 30%, and also proportionately increased its solubility.
lathyrogen treatment of methylcholathrene induced sarcomas in rats reduced the amount of collagen in tumours and increased the solubilization of collagenous components.
the lathyrogen β-aminopropio-nitrile affects collagenous components of tumours of rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of a lathyrogen on the collagenous components of a fibrosarcoma.
the effect of lathyrogenic agent beta-aminopronitrile on the collagenous components of fibrosarcomas.
the effects of a lathyrogen, beta-aminoproprionitrile, on the growth and collagen metabolism of a methylcholanthren-induced fibrosarcomas of rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lathyrogen treatment of tumours has resulted in a reduction in the total collagen content, and a concomitant increase in the extractability of the various collagen fractions.
beta-aminopronipionitrile, the lathyrogen, has a significant effect on the physical and biochemical properties of collagen of methylcholantherine-induced sarcoma of the rat.

lathyrogen has altered the physical properties of tumour collagen, without affecting its growth rate, and this may have important implications for the role of collagenous components in neoplastic growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lathyrogen treatment has affected the collagenous components of the tumours by increasing their solubility and decreasing the amount of total collagen present in the tumour.
the lathyrogenic agent beta-aminopronitrile (BAPN) affects collagen of methylcholantherene-induced fibrosarcomas of rat by increasing the solubility and decreasing the amount of collagen present.
lathyrogen treatment has altered the fibrogenic properties of collagenous components within tumour extracellular matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collagen of tumours of lathyrogen-treated animals is altered in a manner that is qualitatively similar to that of collagen in the skin and tendon of lathyrogen-fed animals.
the collagenous components of fibrosarcomas are affected by the lathyrogen treatment in a manner similar to normal collagenous components.
lathyrogen treatment can be used to study the effect of collagen on the tumour microenvironment and the tumour micro-environment on collagen.
